answers.explanation: Part II is the contractile vacuole, which pumps out excess water from the protozoan.
Part III is the chloroplast-containing region responsible for photosynthesis in the protozoan.
The cell is the lowest level of organisation in living organisms.
The heart is an organ made of several tissues working together, which is a more complex level of organisation than a hair.
The hooks (I) and suckers (III) of the tapeworm attach it to the lining of the host's intestine.
The young proglottid lies close to the neck of the tapeworm, where new segments are formed.
Spirogyra is a filamentous alga made of many cells, unlike the single-celled organisms listed.
In bryophytes the sex organs are produced on the gametophyte generation.
Seed plants dominate the land because their seeds are efficiently dispersed and protected, allowing them to colonise new areas.
Birds live in trees and so are arboreal organisms.
Part I in the transverse section is the cortex, the tissue lying between the epidermis and the vascular tissue.
The diagram shows a dicotyledonous root in transverse section.
The dental formula with incisors, premolars and molars but no canines is characteristic of herbivores such as rabbits.
Amoeba is small enough that diffusion alone can move materials across its body.
Sieve tubes and companion cells are part of the phloem, which transports manufactured food.
Stomata in leaves control gas exchange in the same way as spiracles control gas exchange in insects.
Cutaneous respiration is breathing through the moist skin, which is common in amphibians.
Transpiration is the loss of water vapour from a plant, mainly through the stomata.
A rhizome is an underground stem that survives unfavourable seasons and regrows, so it is an organ of perennation.
Mosses show alternation of generations, with a gametophyte and a sporophyte stage.
Plant growth is apical and continues throughout life, but it has no definite shape, so statements I and III are correct.
Coordination and regulation in mammals are achieved by both the nervous system and hormones.
The cerebellum coordinates muscular activity and balance.
The medulla oblongata controls involuntary actions such as peristalsis in the gut.
A barometer measures atmospheric pressure.
Edaphic factors are influences of the soil on organisms in a habitat.
The genotype is the genetic make-up of an organism, while the phenotype is its observable characteristics.
Light penetration limits photosynthesis and so limits productivity in aquatic habitats.
Primary consumers feed directly on green plants.
Tropical rainforests contain a very large number of plant species.
Population dynamics is the study of how and why population sizes change over time.
The Sahel savanna has the longest and most severe dry season of the savanna zones.
Anabaena is a nitrogen-fixing blue-green alga found in soil.
Clayey soil has the smallest particles and the greatest capacity to retain water.
Poliomyelitis is caused by a virus.
Siting industries away from residential areas reduces the noise that people are exposed to.
Carbon(II) oxide is a toxic constituent of exhaust fumes from generating sets.
Smallpox can be effectively controlled by vaccination.
Nitrogen(IV) oxide dissolves in rain water to form acids, causing acid rain.
Paramecium reproduces by conjugation when the adults become weak, replacing binary fission.
Whorls, arches, loops and compounds are the types of fingerprint variation.
The sex of a child is determined by the sex chromosome carried in the father's sperm, so all children being female points to the father's X chromosome.
Interferon is a biological agent produced by the body that has antiviral properties.
Outbreeding brings together different genetic combinations, which increases disease resistance in the offspring.
Blood group AB is the universal recipient and can receive blood from groups A, B, AB and O.
A streamlined shape reduces water resistance and allows fishes to move easily.
A lizard is poikilothermic, so its body temperature depends on the environment.
Darwin proposed that all living organisms struggle for existence, which drives natural selection.
Adaptive radiation is the diversification of a group into many forms, as shown by the modified mouthparts of insects.
